These align with T-041 mitigations (e): shared staging reservation, free-space reserve, TTL/LRU, and per-donation behavior. There is no production source in this batch, so there is no regression evidence. Integration should verify the SSDWholeRootMaintainer production change that the new tests at head 3140+ exercise. Specifically, if ownership verdicts are cached across passes, a changed file (ctime/size/inode) must be re-verified. This prevents a corrupted or foreign lookalike from being treated as owned and deleted, or an owned file from evading TTL expiry. TTL expiry falls under T-041(b) TTL bound. The new test expects a corrupted header to lose ownership, so the file is not expired. That means non-owned files are left in place rather than deleted, which is a conservative availability choice rather than a confidentiality one.
